session.question: How is the SDG Index used to measur progres toward the SDGs at local and regional level in Romania, and what did the results show?
session.answer:
The SDG Index was used as an indicator-based composite measure to assess progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) at local and regional scales in Romania. The study applied an integrated framework built from 90 indicators, which were stored and processed in a PostgreSQL object-relational database, and then aggregated into an index to compare spatial variation in sustainable development performance across Romanian areas (benedek2021indicator‐basedassessmentof chunk 1). This approach allowed the authors to identify territorial disparities and evaluate how different regions and localities were advancing toward SDG achievement (benedek2021indicator‐basedassessmentof chunk 1).

The results showed strong spatial heterogeneity. The highest sustainable development performance was concentrated in specific geographic areas, whereas rural areas and extended peripheral regions in the eastern and southern parts of Romania performed worst (benedek2021indicator‐basedassessmentof chunk 1). In other words, the index revealed a clear core-periphery pattern in SDG performance, with more favorable outcomes in selected urban or central areas and weaker outcomes in lagging rural and peripheral territories (benedek2021indicator‐basedassessmentof chunk 1).

pqac-99a45373: The excerpt explains that the study evaluates Romania’s regional development from 2000–2020 using sustainability-related indicators, with a focus on child survival, poverty, education, and GDP per capita as measures of prosperity and long-term growth. It emphasizes that these indicators are used to inform regional development policies and assess progress across Romania’s macroregions. The text also notes that the analysis highlights major differences between regions and the importance of public policy in improving sustainability outcomes, such as lowering unemployment and strengthening public services. pqac-90e992e5: The excerpt describes a study that uses a sustainable tourism index (STI), built from 10 statistical indicators selected through principal component analysis (PCA), to assess sustainable tourism development in Romania at a micro-scale (NUTS5/LAU level). It also uses hierarchical ascending classification to examine indicator relationships and territorial disparities. The analysis identifies the most advantaged and disadvantaged areas and shows that tourism performance is strongest in big cities, the Black Sea coast, the Danube Delta, and the Carpathian Mountains. However, the excerpt does not mention an SDG Index or specific local/regional SDG progress results.
From Bianca Mitrică, Paul‐Răzvan Şerban, Irena Mocanu, Nicoleta Damian, Ines Grigorescu, Monica Dumitrașcu, and Cristina Dumitrică. Developing an indicator-based framework to measure sustainable tourism in romania. a territorial approach. Sustainability, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su13052649, doi:10.3390/su13052649.

pqac-ca91d203: The excerpt describes a 2023 study that constructs an aggregate sustainability index in the framework of the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) to compare Central and Eastern European countries. It uses entropy weighting, equal weighting, and principal component analysis to check robustness and also examines countries’ progress toward the SDGs. The results indicate that Balkan countries tend to have lower sustainability levels but higher progress scores, suggesting strong development potential. It also notes that Serbia performs poorly on both sustainability and development potential, and that higher geopolitical risk is associated with lower sustainability.
From Rui Huang. Sdg-oriented sustainability assessment for central and eastern european countries. Environmental and Sustainability Indicators, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.indic.2023.100268, doi:10.1016/j.indic.2023.100268.

pqac-f2125bf9: The excerpt describes a 2022 paper on biosphere-based sustainability in local governments. It explains that the authors assessed Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) interactions in a local governmental context, developed an SDG interaction model, and linked sustainability indicators to the SDGs. The study compared global and local-level interactions and found that while there were some differences at the local level, the overall distribution of synergies and trade-offs was quite coherent. It emphasizes using a local-level assessment aligned with an existing sustainability measurement system to support policymaking and policy coherence. However, it does not mention Romania or the SDG Index specifically.
From Rita Nerland, Heidi Rapp Nilsen, and Bjørn Andersen. Biosphere‐based sustainability in local governments: sustainable development goal interactions and indicators for policymaking. Sustainable Development, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.1002/sd.2371, doi:10.1002/sd.2371.
